not_found.title: No such feature
not_found.description: That feature page doesn't exist — it may have been renamed. Here's everything Discord Analytics actually does.

graphs.title: A ton of graphs
graphs.card_description: Dozens of interactive graphs, ready the moment your bot connects.
graphs.description: Command usage, server growth, active users and votes — already charted, already bucketed, already comparable across any date range you pick.

seo.title: Discord bot graphs and dashboards
seo.description: Interactive graphs for your Discord bot: command usage, server growth, user activity and votes, bucketed hourly or daily over any date range.

graphs.image_alt: The Interactions page showing the evolution of interactions over the last 30 days

pages_section.title: One page per question
pages_section.description: Four pages, each answering a different question about your bot. Nothing to assemble — this is what you see the first time you open the dashboard.

interactions.title: Interactions
interactions.description: Evolution of interactions, most used interactions, most used commands, components and modals, plus type breakdowns for each.

guilds.title: Guilds
guilds.description: Growth over time, additions and removals side by side, distribution by size, and where your servers are — by locale.

users.title: Users
users.description: User and install growth, locale distribution, types of users, and when in the week they're actually active.

votes.title: Votes
votes.description: One evolution chart across every bot list, a split by provider, and a separate chart per provider.

range.title: Pick a range, the buckets follow
range.description: There is no separate "granularity" setting to get wrong. Ranges of a week or less are bucketed hourly; anything longer is bucketed daily, and every chart on the page re-buckets at once.
range.presets: Ten presets ship with it — Today, Yesterday, Last 7 days, Last 30 days, Last 90 days, Month to Date, Last Month, Year to Date, Last 12 Months — plus a custom range if none of them fit.

advanced.title: Rankings, once you opt in
advanced.description: Largest guilds and most active guilds are named lists rather than aggregates, so they only appear once you enable Advanced Stats on your bot.

reports.title: And a summary lands in your inbox
reports.description: You won't open the dashboard every day. A report emails you the same numbers with the previous period drawn underneath, so a flat week is obvious without going looking for it.
reports.image_alt: A report email comparing this week's interactions, guilds and users against last week's

custom_graphs.title: Your bot, your stats
custom_graphs.card_description: Track the events that only matter to your bot.
custom_graphs.description: The built-in graphs cover what every bot does. Custom events cover what yours does — songs queued, tickets opened, images generated, whatever your bot is actually for.

seo.title: Custom events and graphs for Discord bots
seo.description: Send your own events from your Discord bot and get them charted alongside the built-in metrics — no extra tooling, no separate analytics stack.

custom_graphs.image_alt: Three custom event charts: guilds with less than 30 members, tickets created, and reactions under MEE6 messages

form.title: Set up in the dashboard, sent from your code
form.description: You create the event in a dialog — no schema to write, no migration to run — and your bot starts sending it. From that point it behaves like any other chart: same date ranges, same bucketing, same page.

votes.title: All your votes in one place
votes.card_description: Merge every bot-list vote webhook into a single feed.
votes.description: If your bot is on several bot lists, you're running several webhook handlers and reading several dashboards. Point them all at Discord Analytics instead and read one graph.

seo.title: Discord bot vote tracking across bot lists
seo.description: Merge vote webhooks from your bot lists into one feed and one graph, instead of running a handler and reading a dashboard per list.

journey.title: How a vote travels
journey.description: Five bot lists, one secret each, and nothing for you to host in between.

1.title: Someone votes
1.description: On any of the five lists your bot is on.

2.title: The list calls us
2.description: Signed with the secret you configured for that provider.

3.title: It lands in your charts
3.description: Counted in the all-providers total and in that provider's own chart.

4.title: Your community hears about it
4.description: If you set an outgoing webhook, a message is posted.

achievements.title: Time to flex
achievements.card_description: Give your users something to unlock.
achievements.description: Achievements turn your bot's own metrics into goals your users can chase. Craft your own, or copy one that already works from the Community Store.

seo.title: Achievements for Discord bots
seo.description: Turn your Discord bot's metrics into achievements your users can unlock, or copy proven ones from the community store.

achievements.image_alt: Achievement cards showing progress towards their goals

defaults.title: You start with a shelf full
defaults.description: Every bot gets a set of achievements on day one, spanning ten servers to ten thousand. Your users have something to chase before you've written a single one.

2.title: French power 🥖
2.description: Have at least 10% of French-speaking users.

3.title: Old member
3.description: Use Discord Analytics for at least a year.

store.title: Or take one that already works
store.description: The Community Store is achievements other bot owners have published. These are live from the store right now — copy one instead of designing it.

teams.title: A collaborative platform
teams.card_description: Bring your co-maintainers into the dashboard.
teams.description: Bots are rarely a one-person project. Invite the people who maintain yours so they can read the same stats, without sharing your account.

seo.title: Shared team access for Discord bot analytics
seo.description: Invite your co-maintainers to your Discord bot's analytics dashboard so everyone reads the same stats without sharing an account.

1.title: Enter a Discord user ID
1.description: From the Stats Access card on your bot's settings.

2.title: They get an email
2.description: And if we can't reach them, you copy the invitation link instead.

3.title: They sign in with Discord
3.description: Their own account. The invitation expires after 7 days.

4.title: They see the stats
4.description: The same dashboard you're looking at, on that bot only.

access.title: What a teammate can and can't do
access.description: Access is deliberately flat — there are no roles to design, and no permission matrix to audit. A teammate reads; only you administer.

rows.stats: Every stats page — interactions, guilds, users, votes, custom events
rows.settings: Bot settings, API key and votes configuration

scope.title: Per bot, not per account
scope.description: Membership is granted on one bot at a time. A contributor helping on one project doesn't get a window into the others, and removing someone is one click on the same card that invited them.
